description: Fase I1: Dense retrieval failure analysis for q06 and q15

queries.question: How does RAG compare to Fine-tuning (FT) in terms of its suitability for specific tasks?
What characteristic of RAG allows it to achieve strong results without requiring expensive pre-training?

observations: q06 and q15 are both BM25-only gold cases (dense misses gold entirely)
Both queries are short (14-15 words) with high keyword density (0.73-0.79)
Both queries have high domain specificity (RAG/FT comparison, pre-training cost)
Dense top-1 scores for these queries (0.68-0.74) are lower than dense-success queries (0.65-0.78)
No dense-only gold cases exist in this sample — dense adds 0 new recall
hypotheses: HYPOTHESIS: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (general-purpose) may not capture domain-specific semantic relationships for RAG/FT comparison queries
HYPOTHESIS: Short, high-density queries may not provide enough context for dense embedding to match gold chunks
unknowns: Whether a domain-specific dense model would improve q06/q15 retrieval
Whether the dense misses are model limitations or fundamental embedding space issues
